equivalent.label: equivalent

lean-stronger.label: Lean stronger
lean-stronger.meaning: Lean proves a more general statement (e.g. any algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, n ≥ 0); the paper statement is a special case.

partial.label: partial
partial.meaning: Only part of the paper statement, or a neighbouring statement, is formalized.

paper-wrong.label: paper wrong
paper-wrong.meaning: The paper statement is false or ill-typed as printed; Lean proves the corrected statement that the argument actually needs.

unverifiable.label: not checkable here

same.label: same

similar.label: similar

different.label: different

lean-only.label: proved in Lean only

unformalized.label: unformalized

critical.label: critical

major.label: major

minor.label: minor

note.label: note

items.title: Filtrations; Bernstein and order filtrations
items.correspondence: IsFiltration, gr, filtrationDegree and symbol are the printed notions with filtrations indexed by ℕ: F_{-1} = 0 is lowerPiece F 0 = ⊥, and gr = ⊕_j F_j/F_{j-1} is the direct sum of k-modules. filtrationDegree is defined for every a (the least j with a ∈ F_j); the paper defines it for a ≠ 0. The Bernstein and order filtrations are spans of ordered PBW words of bounded weight (isFiltration_bernstein, isFiltration_order), and bernsteinDegree is the filtration degree for B_• (bernsteinDegree_eq: the degree of the Palomar statement). The cited identification gr A_n(k) = k[x, ξ] [Coutinho, Th. 7.3.1] is proved for both filtrations (grEquivSymbolRing), with σ_{i+j}(ab) = σ_i(a)σ_j(b), so gr A_n(k) is commutative.

items.title: Good filtrations
items.correspondence: IsGoodFiltration is Definition 2.4 for the order filtration: a filtration M_• of a right A_n(k)-module M that is compatible with F_• (IsCompatibleFiltration: increasing, exhaustive, M_iF_j ⊆ M_{i+j}, and M_i = 0 for i < 0 through indexing by ℕ) and whose graded module gr M = ⊕_i M_i/M_{i−1} (Support.Gabber.GrModule) is finitely generated over gr A_n = k[x, ξ]. IsCompatibleFiltration is stated for a right module over any filtered algebra, but the gr^F A_n-module structure of gr M, and with it goodness, is formalized only for the order filtration, the only filtration the paper uses for modules. The example is qFilt_isGoodFiltration: for Q = A_n/I the filtration Q_m = qF_m (Support.Gabber.qFilt) is compatible with the order filtration (cyclicFiltration_order_isCompatible) and gr Q is generated by q̄ (Support.Gabber.qFilt_good; gr Q is grCyclic by grCyclicEquiv, generated by q̄ by grCyclic_generated and grCyclic_good).

items.title: Characteristic variety
items.correspondence: CharOf is the printed definition: for a right A_n(k)-module M with a filtration M_•, CharOf M_• = V(Ann_{k[x,ξ]} gr M) ⊆ Spec k[x, ξ], meant for good order filtrations (IsGoodFiltration, Definition 2.4). The last sentence is definition_2_7_independent: two good order filtrations of M give the same set. The paper cites it [HTT, Lemma D.3.1]; Lean proves it along that reference: two good filtrations satisfy F_j ⊆ G_{j+c} and G_j ⊆ F_{j+c'} (Support.Gabber.exists_shift_le), so the radicals of the two annihilators agree (radical_annihilator_eq_of_shift, radical_annihilator_eq_of_good), and V(J) = V(√J). Neither the definition nor the independence needs M finitely generated. Char is the case M = A_n(k)/I with Q_m = qF_m used in Sections 3–6; Char_eq writes it as V(Ann gr Q) with gr Q = grCyclic, and Char_eq_charOf computes it from any good filtration of A_n(k)/I.

items.title: Gabber’s involutivity theorem
items.label: ithm:gabber
items.correspondence: Section2.theorem_2_11 states the theorem as printed: for a field K of characteristic zero and a finitely generated right A_n(K)-module M with a good order filtration (IsGoodFiltration, Definition 2.4: compatible, exhaustive, gr M finite over K[x, ξ]), √(Ann_{K[x,ξ]} gr M) is involutive. The paper cites it [Gab81, SK14, HTT Thm. D.3.4] without proof; the repository proves it by its own route: Support.Gabber.theorem_2_11_general reduces it to cyclic modules (independence of the good filtration, exactness of gr for induced filtrations, induction on the number of generators), and the cyclic case M = A_n(K)/I is GabberGlobalAssembly.associatedGraded_radical_isInvolutive, which follows Gabber and Singh–Kumar (order-Rees ring modulo T², Ore localization at a minimal prime, an Artinian special fibre with a coefficient field, and a trace argument). theorem_2_11_cyclic is the case used in Lemma 4.10 and Section 6.

items.title: Euler grading, A_{≥0} and normality of x₁
items.label: eq:nonnegative-pbw
items.correspondence: Lean defines the grading as printed: eulerDegree is the part of Euler degree m, the eigenspace [E, z] = m z of the commutator [E, ·] (eulerCommutator) with E = x₁p (eulerElement), and the grading is multiplicative (eulerDegree_mul). x₁ has Euler degree 1 (coordinate_mem_eulerDegree), elements commuting with x₁ and p, such as the transverse Weyl algebra, have degree 0 (mem_eulerDegree_zero_of_commute), and a PBW monomial b x₁^a p^c has degree a − c (pairMonomial_mem_eulerDegree). Lean does not state separately for A_n that p has degree −1 or that A_n is the sum of its degree parts; both are used at the pair stage, as the degree a − c of b x₁^a p^c and as the decomposition into homogeneous PBW monomials (mem_iSup_pairWeightSpan). A_{≥0} is the nonnegative part, the sum of the parts of degree m ≥ 0 (nonnegativePart; presentedNonnegativePart in A_n). step_nonnegative_pbw proves that A_{≥0} is generated by the transverse algebra, E and x₁ (WeylEulerSubring.eulerSubring): these lie in A_{≥0} (eulerSubring_le_nonnegativePart), and in PBW form an element of degree m ≥ 0 is a sum of monomials b x₁^a p^c with a − c = m (mem_pairWeightSpan_of_mem_eulerDegree), each in the pair-stage subring generated by the coefficients, x₁ and E (pairWeightSpan_le_eulerSubring), which A_n ≃ PairStage(A_{n−1}) maps into the subring of A_n generated by the transverse algebra, x₁ and E (iterated_eulerSubring_le). eq_nonnegative_pbw gives the four relations (eq:nonnegative-pbw) from p x₁ = x₁ p + 1. step_coordinate_normal derives the normality x₁r = r′x₁ (r, r′ ∈ A_{≥0}) from x₁ commuting with the transverse algebra and the PBW description, and presented_coordinate_normal is the case of A_n. step_positive_mem_nonnegative_mul_coordinate proves that every element of Euler degree ≥ 1 (presentedPositivePart) lies in A_{≥0}x₁: in PBW form b x₁^a p^c = b x₁^{a−c−1} · x₁(x₁^c p^c) with a > c, where x₁^c p^c is a polynomial in E and x₁ crosses it by normality (pairWeightSpan_eq_mul_coordinate).

items.title: Euler products
items.label: lem:euler
items.correspondence: lemma_4_1 states the lemma for x₁ and p = ∂₁ in A_n(k), with E = x₁p: for m ≥ 1, x₁^m p^m = Π_{i=0}^{m−1}(E − i) and p^m x₁^m = Π_{i=1}^{m}(E + i), the products taken in the listed order, and the factors in each product commute. Lean states it for every field k (the characteristic is not used); the paper's n is Lean's n + 1. It is lemma_4_1_of_weylPair, the same identities in any ring with elements x, p such that px = xp + 1, applied to p x₁ = x₁ p + 1 (convention_2_2_relations). The proof is the printed induction: step_4_1_factors_commute, then the induction steps step_4_1_falling_succ (x₁E = (E − 1)x₁, step_4_1_coordinate_shift) and step_4_1_rising_succ (pE = (E + 1)p, step_4_1_momentum_shift).

historical_issues.summary:
Both displayed formulas are shifted for $E=x_1p$. At $m=1$, $x_1p=E$ (the original paper formula gives $E-1$), and $px_1=E+1$ (the original gives $E$). The correct identities are:

$\displaystyle x_1^m p^m=\prod_{i=0}^{m-1}(E-i)$ and $\displaystyle p^m x_1^m=\prod_{i=1}^{m}(E+i)$ (`fallingPoly` and `risingPoly` in Lean).

The original induction silently uses $x_1p=E-1$. Its formulas come from `proof_map` and apply to the convention $E=px_1$. Downstream only disjointness of the roots is used, so the section's conclusion survives.

items.title: Proof of the asymptotic conormal theorem
items.correspondence: theorem_5_7_i_paper is the printed proof of (i), one declaration per paragraph, in the printed order. The algebraic case is step_coordinate_algebraic, the first paragraph: g(x₁) = λ∏(x₁ − c_i), a factor x₁ − c ∈ 𝔭 with c ≠ 0, and dx₁ = d(x₁ − c) conormal at a smooth point of Y (exists_smoothAffinePoint), so (1, 0, …, 0) ∈ N(Y). In the transcendental case the discrete valuation ring V comes from Lemmas 5.9 and 5.10 (generalDivisorialVisibleFrameWithKaehlerFinite through LaneC.divisorialVisibleFrameExistenceWithChart, which calls lemma_5_9 and lemma_5_10; the column is q_a = x̄_a/x̄_j for the chart j of Lemma 5.9), keeping Lemma 5.10(c), Ω_{V/K} finitely generated. Then step_completion (V̂ ≅ κ[[t]], F ↪ κ((t))), step_orders (0 < a < b, j ∉ {0, 1}; a > 0 by Lemma 5.10(a) in step_a_pos), step_generic_point (equation (generic)), Lemma 5.11 at V (witness_lemma_5_11), step_dual_derivations (D_k, Z(t)), step_lambda_w_tau (λ, w = q′ − Zλ = t^c τ), step_M_minor (M(0) has full column rank; a unit minor M_ι), Lemma 5.12(a) at V with m ≤ d′ + 1 by the second fundamental sequence and Nakayama (witness_lemma_5_12_5_13_paper, witness_lemma_5_12_a_bound), step_M_spans_cone (Lemmas 5.12(a), (b)), step_lift_ell_minor (ℓ_υ = u_υ, ℓ_ι = −u_υM_υM_ι⁻¹, ℓM = 0, ℓ(0) = u), step_ell_conormal (Lemma 5.13) and step_polynomial_limit (the final paragraph). One point is done differently: the place is followed by a field E ⊆ V over which κ is finite, which Lean uses to obtain the coefficient field of V̂ (Matsumura Thm. 28.3). The last paragraph, (ii), is step_dir_of_fibre. The terminal theorem GeneralAsymptoticConormal.coordinate_axis_mem_smooth_fibre_closure proves (i) by a second, chart-based route through SameWitness.coordinate_axis_mem_smooth_fibre_closure.

items.correspondence: lemma_5_9: if x̄₁ is transcendental over K, there are a valuation ring W of F with K ⊆ W ≠ F and x̄₁ ∈ 𝔪_W, and an index j with x̄_j ≠ 0 and x̄_i/x̄_j ∈ W for 0 ≤ i ≤ n, where x̄₀ = 1. The proof is the printed one: a valuation ring dominating K[x̄₁] localized at x̄₁ (Stacks Tag 00IA), then j maximal for the preorder x̄_a/x̄_b ∈ W; Definition 5.3(a) enters through definition_5_3 (𝔪_W = W ∖ W^×, and a ∈ W or a⁻¹ ∈ W). The proof of Theorem 5.7 calls it through LaneC.divisorialVisibleFrameExistenceWithChart and takes the column q_a = x̄_a/x̄_j with its chart j.

items.correspondence: lemma_5_10 takes W and j from Lemma 5.9 and gives a discrete valuation ring V of F containing K with (a) q_i ∈ V and x̄₁ ∈ 𝔪_V, (b) κ algebraic over K(res q₀, …, res q_n) and (c) Ω_{V/K} finitely generated, as the fields of Lemma510Place, which also records V = A_{𝔭_D}. Frac V = F holds for every valuation subring of F; the proof also derives it from A ⊆ V as printed. The clause R ⊄ V of (a) is lemma_5_10_a_not_R_le, for every valuation ring with x̄₁ ∈ 𝔪_V; its hypothesis 1 = ḡx̄₁ with ḡ ∈ R is what the paper derives from Y ∩ H = ∅ by the Nullstellensatz. The proof is the printed one: the normalization A of C₀ = K[q₀, …, q_n, x̄₁], a prime 𝔭_D minimal over x̄₁, of height one by Krull’s principal ideal theorem, and V = A_{𝔭_D}, a Noetherian local normal domain of dimension one and hence a discrete valuation ring [Matsumura, Thm. 11.2]; (b) from the integrality of A/𝔭_D over the image of C₀ and (c) by localizing Ω_{A/K}. Definition 5.3 (definition_5_3) gives 𝔪_W = W ∖ W^×. The proof of Theorem 5.7 calls lemma_5_10 through LaneC.divisorialVisibleFrameExistenceWithChart and lemma_5_10_a_not_R_le in step_a_pos.

items.correspondence: lemma_5_11 takes residues r₀, …, r_n ∈ κ with r₀ = r₁ = 0, r_j = 1 and κ algebraic over K(r₀, …, r_n), and gives distinct indices outside {0, 1, j} whose differentials form a basis of Ω_{κ/K}; their number is dim_κ Ω_{κ/K}. The proof is the printed one: the residues with indices outside {0, 1, j} generate L = K(r₀, …, r_n), so they contain a transcendence basis B of L/K (closing sentence of Definition 5.1, definition_5_1_closing; Lang Thm. VIII.1.1); B is a transcendence basis of κ/K because κ/L is algebraic, and in characteristic zero it is a differential basis (Definition 5.1(g), Matsumura Thm. 26.5). witness_lemma_5_11 applies it to the ring V of the proof of Theorem 5.7, which uses the basis in step_dual_derivations.

items.title: Finitely generated torsion modules are cyclic
items.correspondence: Stafford38Challenge.PaperCorollary_6_3 (Challenge.lean, Mathlib-only) states the corollary as printed, and Stafford38.Paper.corollary_6_3 proves it, for every field of characteristic zero and every n. The proof is Section6.corollary_6_3_of, the printed argument: two generators t₁, t₂ and φ(r, s) = t₁r + t₂s (step_6_3_phi_range), a common annihilator d by the right Ore condition (step_6_3_common_annihilator, weyl_rightOreCondition [Björk, Prop. 1.8.4], proved), (a, 1 − Fa) ∈ ker φ (step_6_3_kernel), generation of A_n ⊕ A_n by (a, 1 − Fa) and (1, −F) (step_6_3_generators), and T generated by t₁ − t₂F (step_6_3_pair); corollary_6_3_of also gives stable cyclicity. The input [Sta78, Thm. 3.7] (T is generated by two elements and stably two-generated) is stated as cited, Section6.stafford_1978_theorem_3_7, and proved in the repository by another route than Stafford's: from Theorem 1.1, which does not use Corollary 6.3 (two_generators_of_identity, stably_generated_of_identity). Solution.lean proves PaperCorollary_6_3 through Paper.corollary_6_3; AlternativeSolution.lean through the earlier TorsionCyclicity.weyl_isCyclic_of_isRightTorsion. Stafford38Challenge.PaperCorollary_6_3_stablyCyclic (Challenge.lean, Mathlib-only) states the stable cyclicity of the closing paragraph: every finitely generated torsion right A_n(k)-module T is stably cyclic (IsStablyCyclic: for l ≥ 1 and generators a_1, …, a_{l+1} of T there are f_i with a_i + a_{l+1}f_i, i = 1, …, l, generating T). Stafford38.Paper.corollary_6_3_stablyCyclic proves it as the second component of Section6.corollary_6_3_of: f₁ = −F for l = 1, and the stable two-generation of [Sta78, Thm. 3.7] for l ≥ 2. Solution.lean proves PaperCorollary_6_3_stablyCyclic through Paper.corollary_6_3_stablyCyclic.

Workflow and independent-check claims are provenance, not mathematical consequences. docs/building.md of the formal repository describes the repository verifier and the Comparator replay.

lean_only_intro: Declarations on the path to `Stafford38.universalStatement` (or explicitly off it) that a reviewer meets in Lean but not in the manuscript. They are where the formal proof is more careful than the paper, or takes a different road.

lean_only.name: Stafford38.WeylIteratedEquivalence.presentedIteratedEquiv
lean_only.note: The presented Weyl algebra (RingQuot by `Matrix.J`) is isomorphic to the iterated Ore tower. Euler surjectivity is proved in the tower and transported. The paper silently identifies $A_n = C[p;\partial_1]$ (Convention 3.1).

lean_only.name: Stafford38.WeylEulerRemainder.closure_pairOldSubring_union_coordinate_momentum_eq_top
lean_only.note: “$C$ and $p$ generate $A_n$” — asserted without comment in Proposition 5.3.

lean_only.name: Stafford38.WeylQuotientTransport.transported_canonicalRightIdeal
lean_only.note: Transport of the canonical right ideal between the presentation and the Ore tower.

lean_only.name: Stafford38.WeylOuterOreMonic.presentedOuterPolynomial_monic
lean_only.note: Bernstein-weight PBW monicity ⇒ monic outer Ore polynomial with LEFT coefficients (the paper uses right coefficients $\sum p^j a_j$).

lean_only.name: Stafford.exists_eulerPolynomial_x_pow_mul_d_pow
lean_only.note: This remains a power-multiplication helper in the `proofs` library. The falling and rising Euler-product identities are public theorems in Stafford38/Weyl/EulerProductIdentities.lean; the historical private product lemmas in this file are no longer linked from the manuscript.

lean_only.name: Stafford38.WeylSymplectic.standardSymplecticAlgEquivOfInverse
lean_only.note: Φ is built with an explicit inverse matrix; the paper asserts Φ_g is an automorphism without constructing the inverse.

lean_only.name: Stafford38FixedSourceChallengeTransport.bernsteinDegree_eq
lean_only.note: Identifies the intrinsic “least N with d in span of ordered PBW words of degree ≤ N” with the PBW-normal-form degree used internally.

lean_only.name: Stafford38.CharacteristicAssociatedGradedModule.annihilator_orderAssociatedGradedModule
lean_only.note: Annihilator of gr(A/I) = order initial ideal; together with ξ-homogeneity of the initial ideal this is the fibre-conicality the paper never proves.

lean_only.name: Stafford38.Weyl.FilteredScalarLifting.target_orderInitialIdeal_le_map_source_orderInitialIdeal
lean_only.note: Filtered scalar lifting $\mathrm{in}(I_{\bar k}) \subseteq \mathrm{in}(I)\bar k$: the Lean form of “gr commutes with flat base change” that §10 uses without statement.

lean_only.name: Stafford38.Weyl.FilteredScalarLifting.filteredInitialLifting
lean_only.note: Replaces the paper’s $k_0 \hookrightarrow \mathbb C$ + faithful flatness paragraph: Lean works over `AlgebraicClosure k` and descends the order initial ideal.

lean_only.name: Stafford38.SpecializedNoncharacteristicEquality.transposedSupport_disjoint_axis_iff
lean_only.note: The only place ξ ↦ −ξ enters: the avoidance statement is phrased for the transposed support and transposed straight back. x₁ is fixed by the flip, so nothing changes mathematically.

lean_only.name: Stafford38.SpecializedNoncharacteristicEquality.strictUnitCoordinatePreimage_of_transposedSupport_disjoint_axis
lean_only.note: Consumer turning support avoidance into `orderInitialIdeal ⊔ (x₁) = ⊤` and a strict unit preimage; no paper counterpart.

lean_only.name: AlgebraicAnalysis.FilteredTwoTermPages.FilteredTwoTerm.pointwise_boundary_exhaustion
lean_only.note: The correct exhaustion step of Lemma 6.3: one x₁-preimage taken before localizing kills the class on a later page (the paper’s “iterated preimages” sentence is not a proof).

lean_only.name: AlgebraicAnalysis.exists_uniform_subsingleton_localized
lean_only.note: Uniform page index R after localization (the ACC step of Lemma 6.3).

lean_only.name: Stafford38.Geometry.SmoothAffineConormal.equationConormalClosure_smoothAffine_eq
lean_only.note: For prime I the closure of equation-conormal covectors equals the smooth conormal closure. This is why Lean never needs the paper’s tilted arc.

lean_only.name: Stafford38.Geometry.ConormalScalarExtensionVanishing.scalarExtension_vanishing
lean_only.note: Pulls a conormal direction over a residue/Laurent field back to Dir(Y). Also the missing step in the paper’s Lemma 8.1 (ℂ((t))-point ⇒ Dir(Y)).

lean_only.note: Chart chosen from a valuation ring containing x₁, replacing normalization + properness of the projective closure.

overview: Compare the November 2 frozen manuscript with the pinned Lean results. Every theorem-like statement has a card. In Subsection 5.2 Theorem 5.7 and Lemmas 5.9–5.13 each have their own Lean theorem, and Theorem 5.7 is proved in Lean along the printed route; the earlier chart-based proof is kept as an alternative. Matching conclusions elsewhere do not by themselves certify a printed proof step by step.
how_to_use: Read the paper and Lean proofs side by side. Each passage and declaration links to its exact source. Review tools provide manuscript annotations, all reference passages, and note import/export.
provenance: The paper passages are the November 2 frozen version, pinned and reproduced verbatim. The formal source pins and historical verification receipts are retained. Mathematical edits to the manuscript have not been made by this supplementary update. Comparison labels do not certify a revised printed proof.

    (coeff : k →+* B)
    (fFin : @AlgHom k (MvPolynomial (Option (Fin d)) k) B _ _ _ _ coeff.toAlgebra)

      letI : M.IsMaximal := hM

    {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m)
    (P : PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k))

  hp : Ideal.Quotient.mk P.asIdeal p ≠ 0
  hsmooth : Algebra.Smooth k (Localization.Away fbar)
